title: picasso: self-contained Nix flakes that pin scientific, publishing and agentic toolchains
description: picasso, formerly nix-config, is a set of self-contained Nix flakes, called labs, that pin scientific, publishing and agentic toolchains for other repositories. The ten labs are: WAVEWATCH III with gfortran, OpenMPI and NetCDF (pratico); a pandoc and TeX Live publishing pipeline with its own GitHub Action (publisher); Markdown to PDF for Portuguese in one Rust binary with Typst (ptbr-pdf); a lint set (lint); Markdown papers to PDF and arXiv source (paper); a Gleam toolchain for static sites (gleam-website); a sandbox and helpers for coding agents (agentic); a CUDA cache and PyTorch environment (cuda); a presenter's desk for screen annotation, capture and webcam profiles (present); and a code graph of a repository (viz). Each lab references nothing outside its own directory, commits its lock file and exports the same outputs, so a consumer gets the same pinned toolchain on any machine and in CI: the builds are deterministic, and CI builds every lab's checks in the Nix sandbox on every push. The code is only Nix and Rust: the repository tools are one Rust workspace and the lab tools are Rust crates. The smallest result is ptbr-pdf: the same Markdown-to-PDF job needs 729 MiB with pandoc and XeLaTeX and 25.2 MiB as one static Rust and Typst binary. picasso is the toolchain layer under WW3 GPU Lab, marola, ptbr-writer and other repositories, which borrow a lab as a flake input, a sparse git submodule or a GitHub Action.

creators.name: Hoffmann, Matheus

notes: Consumers: WW3 GPU Lab (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23221351, github.com/h0ffmann/ww3-gpu) uses the pratico, publisher and gleam-website labs; marola (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23224155) uses the lint and agentic labs; ptbr-writer (github.com/h0ffmann/ptbr-writer) uses ptbr-pdf and gleam-website. The repository layout and README style follow gvolpe/nix-config by Gabriel Volpe. The name is a homage to Pablo Picasso's one-line drawings and implies no affiliation with the Picasso estate; the logo and drawings are original.
